---
title: Tools and statuses
description: The six actions an agent can request, the rules every request must follow, and what each status means.
---

Each action is one HTTP request naming a tool, its arguments, a reason, and a `client_id`. The customer sees the exact command, path or host first, with your reason underneath as yours.

```json
{
  "tool": "read_file",
  "args": { "path": "~/Library/Logs/AcmeApp/main.log" },
  "reason": "Read the app's log to see the error from the last launch.",
  "client_id": "4f1c2a9e0b7d4e6a"
}
```

## Tools

Prefer a structured tool over `run_command` whenever one fits. Structured tools need no program permission and can't be stopped partway by the sandbox.

| Tool | Arguments | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `list_processes` | none (`{}`) | `{ processes: [{ pid, name }] }` |
| `read_file` | `path`, `max_bytes` (optional) | `{ content, hash, truncated }` |
| `tail_log` | `path`, `lines` (optional, 1 to 5000) | `{ content, hash }` |
| `list_dir` | `path` | `{ entries: [{ name, type, size }], truncated }` |
| `run_command` | `command` (list of strings), `cwd` (optional) | `{ exit_code, stdout, stderr, truncated }` |
| `write_file` | `path`, `content`, `base_hash` | `{ hash, bytes }` |

### `run_command`

`command` is a list of arguments, not a shell string. The first item is the program: an absolute path, or a bare name such as `ls` looked up in `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/sbin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin`.

```json
{ "tool": "run_command", "args": { "command": ["/usr/sbin/system_profiler", "SPSoftwareDataType"] } }
```

Other items are passed as they are: `~` and `$VARS` are not expanded, so give absolute paths. For a pipeline, send `["/bin/sh", "-c", "…"]`. The customer sees exactly that, and it needs `/bin/sh` allowed.

### `write_file`

`write_file` replaces a whole file. `base_hash` must be the `hash` from your latest `read_file` or `tail_log` of that file. If the file changed since, the write is `rejected`, so read it again. To create a new file, send the hash of empty content:

```text
e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
```

## Rules every request follows

These are checked before anyone is asked. Breaking one returns HTTP 400 `invalid_request`, with a `hint` naming the field, or the status `rejected`.

- `args` is always an object. A tool with no arguments takes `{}`.
- `reason` is 1 to 500 characters.
- `client_id` is 8 to 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`, new for each action. Resending the same `client_id` never runs an action twice, so it is safe to retry after a dropped connection.
- `path` and `cwd` start with `/` or `~/` and contain no `..`. `~` is the customer's home folder.
- `command` is a list of 1 to 64 strings.

## What can't run

- Commands run in a sandbox. They can read only the files, and start only the programs, the customer allowed. A `cwd` asks to read that folder.
- macOS won't start programs with raised privileges (such as `sudo`, `su` and `ps`) inside a sandbox. They are `rejected` before the customer is asked. Use `list_processes` instead of `ps`.
- macOS's `log` command refuses to run in a sandbox. Read log files with `tail_log`.

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | Covered by a permission, and done | Use the output |
| `approved` | The customer allowed it when asked, and it ran | Use the output |
| `pending` | Waiting for the customer | Wait for it again |
| `denied` | The customer said no, or the sandbox stopped it partway | Don't send it again. Find another way within what's allowed |
| `rejected` | Turned back before anyone was asked, such as a stale `base_hash` | Fix the request |
| `failed` | It ran but couldn't finish | Read `error` |
| `ended` | The session ended first | Stop |

A `denied` whose `error` starts with `sandbox:` means the program tried to reach something not allowed. It is not the customer saying no. Read `stderr` to see what it needed, and ask for that with a structured tool.

Every answer also carries `events`: what else changed since you last looked, such as `grants.changed`, `session.extended` or `session.ended`.
